messages:
harper: FYI we're seeing a surge in gpu attach latencies in eu-west3 starting ~1768012200. pods pending because kube attach to gnodes times out.
jin: getting high iowait on local NVMe during batch window. overlayfs gc kicked off and IOPS shot up to 120k on nvme1 :grimacing:
leo: spotted `blkld` stall traces and lots of device_resets in dmesg on gnode-2{3,7,9}. could be controller busy -> detach/attach races.
ops-bot: [alert] region=eu-west3 metric=nvme.iops spike=120k hosts=9 severity=high
harper: symptoms: new pods keep requeuing, scheduler backs off, net result is GPU queue grows and customer latency rises.
jin: quick check: janitor scheduled deep-clean across hosts during our nightly batch overlap. command that ran: ```/srv/janitor/run.sh --clean-level=deep --hosts=eu-west3 --parallel=6```
leo: that deep-clean uses lots of small random writes (overlayfs prune) which destroys queue depth headroom. GPUs attach needs stable io ops to finish init.
fin: can we throttle janitor concurrency or shift it to cold hours? product asked for minimal impact windows but we need a pragmatic temporary exception.
harper: short-term mitigation list I propose:
- reduce janitor parallelism to 1 in eu-west3
- pause deep-clean tasks for 2 hours
- temporarily disable prefetch/overlay_gc on hosts with GPUs scheduled
- spin up 10 reserved warm GPUs in eu-west1 and route lower-priority jobs there
- collect iostat/sar and attach latency metrics for 3h
jin: executed throttle: ```/bin/janitorctl scale --region eu-west3 --parallel 1 --task deep-clean```
ops-bot: action=janitor.scale status=ok region=eu-west3 parallel=1 task=deep-clean
leo: I'm evicting nonessential pods from 9 hot hosts (graceful 5m). starting with gnode-23,27,31. using: ```bin/node-drain --node gnode-23 --grace 300s --filter noncritical```
fin: cost tradeoff: if we shift 10 reserved GPUs across regions it's ~+7% for 6 hours. Product ok with that if it avoids SLA hits.
harper: routing change done: added eu-west1 reserved pool and updated load balancer rule to prefer it for best-effort jobs. link: https://infra/redwood/routing/1768012410
jin: after throttle attach success improved from 62% -> 93% in first 10m. iostat shows nvme1 ops dropped to 18k and avg await down from 28ms -> 4ms.
leo: still seeing occasional controller resets on gnode-27; planning to repro with reduced scrub to see if firmware interacts with overlayfs workload. scheduling fw-check on the host.
ops-bot: event=controller.reset host=gnode-27 time=1768012558
harper: agreed next steps:
- keep deep-clean paused til spike resolves (~2h)
- ops to run fw-health job on hosts showing resets
- infra to consider IOQ limit per janitor job (longer term)
- finance notified about temporary reserved shift (cc @fin)
jin: I'll follow up with histograms and attach latency dashboards; will put a short blameless note in #postmortems if we confirm overlap root cause.
fin: tracking the spend in the incident sheet, tagging as temporary spike.
leo: thanks everyone — signal improving, will monitor for 90m then close thread.
